question: Is the fixed-a strongly-filtered k^2 gradient expansion used in C10.50-C10.54 uniformly compatible with the already-certified history-wide M_c window over the declared cosmological EFT domain, despite the noncommuting formal limits k->0 and a->0?

scope.history_window: M_c^2>=99 k_cos_phys^2 on the declared EFT history, with each audited cosmological mode satisfying k_phys^2<=k_cos_phys^2
scope.EFT_onset: finite declared a_EFT>0; no extrapolation to an arbitrarily early a->0 UV regime

acceptance: prove lim_{k->0 at fixed a,M_c} a1_eff=0 and lim_{a->0 at fixed k,M_c} a1_eff=1, so the two formal limits do not commute
define z=k_phys^2/M_c^2; from M_c^2>=99 k_cos_phys^2 and k_phys^2<=k_cos_phys^2 prove 0<=z<=1/99
prove a1_eff=z/(1+z)<=1/100 over the audited cosmological EFT domain
rewrite K_hat=-(3/(2M_c^2))/(1+z) and show its O(z) expansion K0(1-z) has exact relative truncation error z^2<=1/9801
show the leading approximation a1_eff~z has relative error z<=1/99, while all C10 projector calculations continue to use the exact filter rather than this approximation
classify the C10.50-C10.54 fixed-a k^2 expansion as uniformly controlled on the declared strong-filter EFT window, not as a theorem extending to a->0 before EFT onset
emit an immutable machine-checked certificate without selecting numerical M_c or a_EFT
next_if_pass: derive the physical baseline-species O(k^2) adiabatic coefficient C2 on the finite EFT-onset strongly-filtered branch and project B0 with the C10.54 formula.
non_claims: does not select numerical M_c, lambda_HL, eta0 or a_EFT
does not extend the IR completion arbitrarily to a->0
does not derive the species adiabatic coefficient C2
does not implement completed-U1 CLASS feedback or spectra
